Oil is **down**, so the Hormuz-style risk-off overlay does **not** fire. 08-27 leftover: NVDA/CRM are **not** XLF holdings; do not map residual AI beta into S0+.

Live factor is **rotation out of financials** (08-27: only tech of 11 S&P sectors up; XLF −0.65% vs SPY +0.66%; BKX −0.56%). IB/trading “fee boom” is **stale Q2** — do not treat as structural NIM. **4. Breadth / leadership**  
1d and 3d relative are **decisively red**. 1w residual +0.52% is the leftover streak, not live leadership. Large-caps (JPM/BKX) participated in the lag — not ETF-only. 1m rel −3.59% = cyclical laggard vs SPY.

**5. Flows / crowding**  
XLF **outflows**: ~−$494M (08-24), ~−$247M (08-25); Trefis ~**−$2B** past month. July inflows have reversed. That is de-allocation after an extended bid, not a fresh inflow spike.

**6. Catalysts**  
No 8:30 high-impact US print. **Warsh 10:00 ET**, Chicago PMI 9:45, UMich final 10:00. Two-sided policy event **caps magnitude**; it does not authorize an up call into a red 1d/3d tape.

- **08-27 Financial:** NVDA already public; do **not** call up off a broken streak. Today S4 is **negative**, not flat → absolute **down**, band **mild**.

- **08-21 mag:** one band; rolling mag 0.2 → **mild**, not notable.
- Rotation/fade scored **once** in S2, half in S3, S4 confirmation only.

## 0. Facts
XLF **+0.38%** (open 57.98 → close 58.10). SPY **−0.23%**. Relative **+0.61%**. Absolute **up / mild**. Path: modest green from the open (pre-market ~58.02), held a 57.92–58.41 range, closed 58.09–58.10. Not a crash, not a melt-up.

Morning call to beat: **down / flat**, total **−2.925**, S0 0 / S1 0 / S2 −1 / S3 −0.5 / S4 −1, Warsh treated as a two-sided mag-cap, leftover 08-27 tape treated as rotation-*out*.

## 1. What drove the sector
Primary driver was **policy-path, not credit**. Warsh’s first JH as Chair was read hawkish: inflation still the job, summer PCE/CPI “better than expected” but **not** a meaningful trend break, “we have work to do.” Sep 25 bp hike odds jumped from ~35% to ~56–58%. The **2Y led** (+~12 bp to 4.356%); 10Y +~5 bp to 4.726%; 30Y only +~2 bp to 5.211%. That is **short-end flattening**, not the 08-17 long-end/term-premium steepener the morning correctly refused to score as NIM+.

Credit did **not** blow out (HY OAS last print **2.63%** on 08-27, still tight). VIX stayed calm. Equities: S&P ~−0.25%, Nasdaq ~−0.52%. Financials were the **relative** bid vs a tech/Nasdaq fade — the inverse of 08-27 (then only tech of 11 sectors up; XLF −0.65% / rel −1.31%).

Inside the sector: **large-cap banks** participated (BKX last **187.17**, ~+0.3%; JPM ~+0.8–0.9%; WFC ~+2%). **GS** lagged (~−0.5% to −0.7%). Regionals (KRX) reported ~−0.26%. So this was money-center / XLF-beta leadership, not a regional-bank stress bounce and not an IB/trading surge.

Chicago PMI **47.1** (year-weak, vs ~57–59 expected) and UMich final **51.7** were same-morning prints; they did not dominate XLF vs the Warsh short-end repricing.

Taxonomy: **HIT** — hawkish policy / real-yield/short-end up, rotation *into* financials vs SPY, credit still tight. **MISS** vs morning — risk-off, credit blowout, long-end NIM steepener, deposit/CRE spike.

## 2. Audit morning S0–S4 (use morning numbers, do not rewrite them)
| Sleeve | Morning | Reality | Verdict |
|---|---|---|---|
| **S0 0** | Not credit risk-off; not financials risk-on; PCE already in; Warsh two-sided | Hawkish resolution, short-end up, SPY red, XLF green; credit still tight | **Sign miss after 10:00 ET**, but **0 was the honest pre-speech score**. The error was using leftover tape as if S0 were already signed down. |
| **S1 0** | 2s10s ~+47 bp = long-end headwind ≠ NIM+; HY tight; NIM/credit quality carried | Curve **flattened** via 2Y, not a bull-steepener; hike-odds is a *different* NIM story than 08-17 | **08-17 lesson held.** Did not false-score long-end as NIM+. Did not pre-score hawkish Warsh as NIM+ either — correct at open, incomplete after the print. |
| **S2 −1** | 1d/3d rel red; rotation *out* | 1d rel **+0.61%** (≥ +0.4% 08-18 trigger); BKX/JPM/WFC up | **Stale.** Scored yesterday’s rotation as today’s breadth. |
| **S3 −0.5** | XLF outflows 08-24/25, ~−$2B 1m | No evidence flows flipped the session; volume ~25M, not a squeeze | **Not falsified, not the driver.** Half-weight leftover de-allocation did not cap a +0.38% day. |
| **S4 −1** | 08-27 XLF −0.65% / rel −1.31% | Today +0.38% / rel +0.61% | **Lagged tape, then reversed.** Same class of error as 08-27’s “don’t call up off a broken streak,” inverted. |

Pipeline **down/flat** vs actual **up/mild**: **direction miss**, magnitude not far from the flat band (0.38% is barely mild). Confidence 0.52 was appropriately modest; the signed down call was not.

## 3. Interactions / double-count / knowable-at-open
**Double-count:** Rotation-out was stacked in **S2, S3, and S4** off the **same 08-27 leftover**. When that leftover mean-reverted, all three flipped together. That is not three independent down votes.

**Not double-counted (good):** July PCE, NVDA/CRM AI beta, Q2 IB haul, ALL/AON/VCTR names. Those stayed out.

**Knowable at open:** Warsh 10:00 ET as the live binary; no 8:30 print; credit tight; long-end ≠ NIM+; 1d/3d tape was red. **Not knowable:** hawkish *resolution*, 2Y +12 bp, Sep hike ~35%→~57%, Nasdaq fade vs banks. Morning used the binary only as a **magnitude cap** while letting stale S2/S4 dictate **direction**. That fails the knowable-at-open test for the down call.

**08-18:** Today’s rel **+0.61%** *does* fire rotation-into-banks. It was **not** live at the open (1d rel was −1.31%). Do not rewrite the morning as if it should have called up.

**08-21 mag-temper:** One band was right; actual is mild, not notable.

## 4. Outliers inside the sector
- **WFC ~+2%** vs XLF +0.38% — large-cap bank outlier to the upside.
- **GS ~−0.5% to −0.7%** — IB/markets name did not ride the NIM/hike tape; GSIB fight remains noise, not the ETF.
- **KRX ~−0.26% vs BKX ~+0.3%** — regionals did not confirm; this was not a KRE-style catch-up.
- **Nasdaq ~−0.52% vs XLF +0.38%** — 08-27 tech-only leadership reversed in one session.
